sentence: This project studies how aging changes the blood system and looks for ways to keep it healthy during aging.
This project studies how mutations in the untranslated regions of RNAs disrupt protein production in neurodevelopmental disorders.
This project studies the molecular steps behind microglial infiltration in glioblastoma and develops therapies that target it.
This project builds gene editing tools that find and remove the repeat-bearing transcripts of a gene that causes amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
This project tests a small chemical molecule as a therapy for ovarian cancer in preclinical models.
This project runs research projects that study prostate cancer biology and treatment, focusing on advanced castration-resistant prostate cancer.
This project uses a rabies virus with and without mutations to study how neuron immune signaling shapes viral spread in the brain.
This project studies how the human heart's natural pacemaker develops by finding the genes and signals that guide its formation.
This project checks the quality of laboratory tests for HIV and related viruses used in clinical studies.
This project studies how anhedonia, a loss of interest or pleasure, passes from parents to early adolescents through neurophysiological and behavioral pathways.
This project uses mouse and human genetics to study how the craniofacial skeleton develops and is maintained.
This project studies why immune checkpoint inhibitors cause severe toxicity in melanoma patients and builds an assay to predict it.
This project provides mass spectrometry, histology and imaging support to investigators using tissue and cell-based models.
This project uses artificial intelligence with chest computed tomography and chest-X-rays to diagnose early tuberculosis disease.
This project tries to engineer human heart tissue that can regenerate and repair the heart.
This project builds ingestible sensors that detect disease activity in the intestine and release reporters that are exhaled to detect colorectal cancer.
This project combines experiments and biophysical modeling to predict how pathogens become resistant to antibiotics and other drugs.
This project studies how heavy metals, endocrine-disrupting chemicals and prenatal folic acid affect RNA modifications and DNA methylation in autism, using brain organoids.
This project tries to find out how healthy cells control levels of an inositol lipid and link them to membrane functions.
This project studies how artificial intelligence image enhancement tools can add false or misleading features to positron emission tomography images.
